fullName: RRB JE — Junior Engineer, Depot Material Superintendent and Chemical & Metallurgical Assistant
overview: RRB JE is the Railway Recruitment Boards' recruitment for the **technical, field and workshop posts of Indian Railways**: **Junior Engineer** in the electrical, civil, mechanical and S&T (signals and telecom) departments, **Depot Material Superintendent (DMS)** in stores, and — added through corrigendum in the 2026 cycle — **Chemical & Metallurgical Assistant (CMA)**. The selection runs in two computer-based stages: **CBT 1 (screening) → CBT 2 (merit) → document verification → medical examination**, with **no interview**. CBT 1 is a common paper for everyone (Maths, Reasoning, General Awareness, General Science), while CBT 2 adds a heavy **Technical Abilities paper of 100 questions from your own engineering branch**. That technical paper is what separates this exam from NTPC and Group D: the general subjects are standard competitive-exam fare, but the 100-question branch paper decides the merit, so your diploma or degree subjects carry most of the weight. Pay is **Level 6 (initial pay ₹35,400)** for every post in the current cycle, and the medical standard for most posts is **B-1 or B-2**, so vision and fitness matter — check the post parameters before you commit.

Age is counted as on **1 January 2027**. Apply only through the official RRB websites and rrbapply.gov.in.

stages.name: CBT 1 — First Stage (screening)
stages.notes: One 90-minute block (120 minutes for scribe-eligible candidates), no sectional timing. Within the 45 General questions the CEN table splits **General Science 30** (Physics, Chemistry and Life Sciences up to 10th standard CBSE) and **General Awareness 15** (current affairs, geography, history including the freedom struggle, polity and constitution, economy, environmental issues, sports, scientific and technological developments). Minimum qualifying marks: **UR and EWS 40%, OBC-NCL and SC 30%, ST 25%** (relaxable by 2 marks for PwBD candidates against a shortage). Normalised scores are used only to shortlist for CBT 2, at **15 times the community-wise vacancies** of the RRB (the RRB can change this ratio). CBT 1 marks do **not** count in the final merit.

stages.name: CBT 2 — Second Stage (merit-deciding)

sections.name: Common part: General Awareness, Physics & Chemistry, Basics of Computers, Environment & Pollution Control

stages.notes: **150 questions in 120 minutes (160 for scribe-eligible candidates); a virtual calculator is available on screen.** The common part of 50 questions splits as **General Awareness 15, Physics & Chemistry 15 (up to 10th standard CBSE), Basics of Computers and Applications 10, Basics of Environment and Pollution Control 10**. The remaining **100 questions are Technical Abilities from your Exam Group**, decided by your qualification: Mechanical and Allied, Electrical and Allied, Electronics and Allied, or Civil and Allied Engineering (Annexure VIII A to D of the CEN), or the separate CMA group (Physics and Chemistry, Annexure VIII E). Diploma holders with more than one qualifying branch choose one Exam Group but can then be considered for all posts they opted for. Minimum qualifying percentages are the same as CBT 1 (UR/EWS 40%, OBC-NCL and SC 30%, ST 25%). Shortlisting for document verification is based on CBT 2 merit, expressed as a **Merit Index** scored from 350 (at the general-category qualifying mark of 40) up to 900 (at the mean of the top 0.1% of candidates), so candidates of different branches compete on one common scale. The site's technical-section practice lives under your branch's engineering subjects; the GA section covers the common part.

stages.name: Document Verification and Medical Examination
stages.notes: Candidates are shortlisted for DV **RRB-wise at 1:1 of the vacancies**, on normalised CBT 2 merit and post options. Ties are broken first by **age (the older candidate ranks higher)** and then alphabetically by given name. At DV you produce all original certificates — qualification, date of birth, category, and an NOC if you are a serving government or PSU employee; failure to produce originals forfeits the candidature. Appointment depends on clearing the railway **medical examination** against the standard of your post: most JE posts carry **B-1 or B-2**, some carry **C-1**, and a few design posts carry **A-3** (for A-3 posts, candidates who have had LASIK or similar refractive surgery are not eligible; colour, binocular and night vision tests apply). A one-time medical appeal with prescribed charges is allowed if you fail the initial medical. There is no interview anywhere in the process.

eligibility.notes: Qualifications must be **complete on or before the closing date** (13 September 2026 for CEN 04/2026); candidates awaiting results cannot apply. Relaxations are **not cumulative** — if you qualify on more than one ground you get the maximum of them, and SC, ST and OBC-NCL candidates against UR vacancies get no relaxation. Age limits for the posts are uniform in this cycle because every post is Level 6; earlier cycles (CEN 03/2024) had 18 to 36 years for all posts as a one-time Covid relaxation of 3 years over the standard 18 to 33. The detailed CEN of the cycle you apply in is the final word.

selectionProcess: **CBT 1 (screening) → CBT 2 (merit) → Document Verification → Medical Examination. No interview.** CBT 1 shortlists candidates for CBT 2 at 15 times the community-wise vacancies of each RRB, on normalised marks. The final merit is built **only from CBT 2**, expressed as a Merit Index between 350 and 900 so that candidates from different Exam Groups compete on a common scale for the same posts. DV shortlists are drawn RRB-wise at 1:1 of the vacancies, with ties broken by age (older first) and then alphabetically. Every post is Level 6, and post and zone allotment follow merit, options, medical fitness and vacancy position.
normalization: Both CBTs are held over multiple days and shifts with different question papers, so raw marks are **normalised across shifts** before any shortlisting, using the RRBs' published method. For the final merit the normalised (or raw, for single-session) marks are then converted into a **Merit Index**: the general-category qualifying mark of 40 maps to 350, and the mean marks of the top 0.1% of candidates (or top 10, whichever is larger) maps to 900. In practice: never compare raw scores with friends in other shifts; a tougher paper is statistically adjusted in your favour; and the merit index, not your raw total, decides the panel.

faqs.q: Is there negative marking in RRB JE?
faqs.a: Yes. **1/3 mark is deducted for every wrong answer** in both CBT 1 and CBT 2, while each correct answer earns 1 mark. Unattempted questions cost nothing.

faqs.q: What is the CBT 1 and CBT 2 pattern?
faqs.a: **CBT 1:** 100 questions in 90 minutes — Mathematics 30, General Intelligence & Reasoning 25, General Awareness 15, General Science 30. **CBT 2:** 150 questions in 120 minutes — General Awareness 15, Physics & Chemistry 15, Basics of Computers and Applications 10, Basics of Environment and Pollution Control 10 and **Technical Abilities 100** from your branch. A virtual calculator is available in CBT 2. The CEN says the section-wise splits are indicative and may vary slightly in actual papers.

faqs.q: Does CBT 1 count towards the final merit?
faqs.a: No. CBT 1 is purely a screening test. Its normalised score is used only to shortlist candidates for CBT 2 at **15 times the community-wise vacancies** of each RRB, subject to the category-wise minimum percentages. The final merit is built **only from CBT 2**.

faqs.q: What is the Technical Abilities paper and which branch will I get?
faqs.a: The last 100 questions of CBT 2 come from your **Exam Group**, fixed by your qualification: **Mechanical and Allied, Electrical and Allied, Electronics and Allied, or Civil and Allied Engineering**, or the separate **CMA group** for B.Sc Physics and Chemistry candidates. Diploma holders eligible through more than one branch choose one Exam Group during the application, but remain eligible for all the posts they opted for. The group-wise syllabus is given in Annexure VIII of the CEN.

faqs.q: What is the Merit Index and why is my score out of 900?
faqs.a: Because candidates from different branches compete for the same posts, RRB converts normalised CBT 2 marks into a common **Merit Index**: the general-category qualifying mark (40) maps to **350** and the mean marks of the top 0.1% of candidates (or top 10, whichever is larger) maps to **900**. DV shortlists and panel merit are decided on this index, which is why official cutoffs after CBT 2 look like 700 to 800 rather than marks out of 150.

faqs.q: What is the qualification for RRB JE posts?
faqs.a: **JE:** three-year engineering diploma in the relevant branch (Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics, Civil or a listed combination); a B.E./B.Tech or higher degree in the same discipline is accepted in lieu of the diploma. **DMS:** three-year diploma in any engineering discipline (degree accepted in lieu). **CMA:** B.Sc in Physics and Chemistry with at least 45% marks. Qualifications must be complete before the application closing date; candidates awaiting results cannot apply.

faqs.q: What is the age limit and the cut-off date for the 2026 cycle?
faqs.a: **18 to 33 years as on 1 January 2027** for all posts in CEN 04/2026 (all are Level 6). Standard relaxations apply: OBC-NCL +3 years, SC/ST +5 years, plus separate limits for ex-servicemen, PwBD, serving railway staff, and widowed or divorced women as given in the CEN table. (In CEN 03/2024 the limit was 18 to 36 years because of a one-time 3-year Covid relaxation.)

faqs.q: What is the application fee and how does the refund work?
faqs.a: **₹500** for all other candidates, of which **₹400 is refunded (minus bank charges) after you appear in CBT 1**; **₹250** for SC, ST, ex-servicemen, PwBD, female, transgender, minority and EBC candidates, **fully refunded after you appear**. Only candidates who actually attend CBT 1 get the refund. Changing application details later costs a **₹250 modification fee per occasion**.

faqs.q: Can I raise objections against the answer key?
faqs.a: Yes. After each CBT the RRBs open a window to view your questions, responses and the provisional keys, and objections can be raised online for a **fee of ₹50 plus bank charges per question**. If your objection is found correct, the fee for that question is refunded. The RRBs' decision on objections is final.

faqs.q: Which posts and medical standards should I check before applying?
faqs.a: Every post in the current cycle is **Level 6 (₹35,400)**, so pay does not differ — the differences are department, posting and medical standard. Most JE posts need **B-1 or B-2**, some design posts need **A-3** (where LASIK or similar refractive surgery disqualifies you), and CMA needs **B-1**. Check Annexure A (post parameters) for the standard of each post, because failing the medical means no appointment on that post and no alternative.

documents: Keep these ready for the application and for **Document Verification**: **Class 10 (matriculation) certificate** as date of birth and name proof, **diploma or degree certificates with all semester/year marksheets** (or the B.Sc certificate for CMA) with the date of issue or result declaration, **category certificate** in the central government format (OBC-NCL, EWS, SC or ST), **EBC certificate (Annexure III-A), BPL card or Izzat MST** if you claimed the fee concession, **ex-servicemen and PwBD certificates** where applicable, an **NOC from your employer** if you are serving in a central or state government department or PSU, a **valid photo ID** (Aadhaar is strongly preferred, since Aadhaar-linked biometric authentication is used at the exam centre), the **live photograph** captured during the application, and your scanned **signature**. Name or date of birth mismatches across documents are the commonest cause of DV trouble — fix them with a gazette notification before you apply. SC and ST candidates who opt for the **free sleeper-class train pass** must carry the original caste certificate at every stage.
